newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong protester saved by Japanese medics.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong protester saved by Japanese medics.

text.p: Hong Kong activist David Chan has been saved by a Japanese first-aid team, after a television report that he had been feared drowned in a protest dive in the East China Sea, Hong Kong Commercial Radio reported on Thursday.
"After reviving by a team of Japanese medical team, (David) Chan has a weak heartbeat," the Commercial Radio, which has a correspondent on board the protest ship Kien Hwa 2, said.
The ship was now heading to a Japanese island to get medical treatment for Chan, the radio said.
There was no immediate confirmation from other sources.

Earlier, Hong Kong Cable TV and government radio quoted correspondents on board as saying Chan was feared dead and another activist was flown away for medical treatment by a Japanese helicopter after they dived into the sea.

"When he (David Chan) was pulled out of the water he had no heartbeat or pulse," Hong Kong Cable TV reported. The two were among five activists who dived into the sea in protest against Japanese control of the islands, which are also claimed by China.
